policy.purpose: prevent any retry, delayed job or surviving writer from silently recreating erased prepared intelligence inside the erased Brain scope
policy.retention_rule: retain the minimal tombstone while its workspace Brain scope exists; remove it with the complete workspace closure
policy.expiry_rule: no tombstone expiry inside a continuing workspace because expiry would reopen silent revival
policy.reconsent_rule: never clear or overwrite an erasure tombstone; explicit subject reconsent creates a new workspace and custody scope after a separate consent receipt is durably accepted
policy.old_scope_rule: the erased scope remains erased and can return only status metadata with zero protected items
policy.access_rule: service-only, no browser table access, no protected payload, no evidence excerpts and no model use
policy.backup_rule: restored data must reapply the erasure state before any prepared-intelligence writer or reader is enabled
policy.review_rule: review purpose necessity at least annually and on every privacy-policy or deletion-flow change

allowed: workspace, custody and stable subject scope identifiers

current_candidate_alignment: one tombstone is unique per workspace and subject
workspace and custody deletion cascade to the tombstone
stable subject deletion is restricted while the scope exists
both legacy and custody writers reject erased scope
browser roles receive no tombstone table access
R31 returns erased with zero items

external_basis.use: retention must have a necessary stated purpose, a documented rule and periodic review

external_basis.use: backup data must be put beyond use and the restoration process must preserve erasure
